scope: Research prototype only. Adds a sanitiser (protocol §2 producer) and a leak verifier (§2.4) for plan-071 Suggested-post captures. Modifies no production file and no file under plans/research/068/ or /071/.
summary: Plan 071 asks a contributor to hand-sanitise real markup and to state the exact grep proving no real name, sentence or URN remains. Plan 071's own gate does not verify that sanitisation happened. This plan mechanises both halves and proves end to end that sanitised output is admissible to the unmodified 071 gate without destroying the detector signal.

stepZeroFinding.claim: The plan-071 'sanitization:' gate accepts an entry that still contains a person's name, a full post body, a global id attribute, a profile slug with a tracking parameter, a srcset, and identifying alt text.
stepZeroFinding.method: Ran the exact content assertions from plans/research/071/probe-extensions.test.cjs against a crafted PII-shaped entry; the gate's only content check is a urn sentinel prefix.
stepZeroFinding.result: gate passed: true; 7 of 7 PII-shaped classes survived
stepZeroFinding.note: All values in the demonstration are invented. This is a gap in gate coverage, not a claim that any real capture was ever leaked.

sanitize.cjs.failClosedTrigger: unterminated quoted attribute, unterminated comment or tag, unparsable tag syntax, or any structural fingerprint mismatch — all return an error and NO markup; there is no override flag

protocolRules.§2.1 text: every alphanumeric run becomes 'Placeholder'; the declared --label, punctuation-only tokens such as '·', and surrounding whitespace survive; consecutive placeholders collapse to one
protocolRules.§2.2 structure: element names, class values and nesting are enforced identical by comparing a structural fingerprint of input vs output before emitting
protocolRules.§2.3 identity: drops id/nonce/integrity/crossorigin/referrerpolicy/srcset/imagesrcset/data-urn/ping/on*/data-tracking*/data-trk*/data-impression*/data-*-ref/data-*-id/style; strips URL query and fragment; rewrites in|company|school|showcase|groups slugs; sentinelises urn:li payloads in ANY attribute incl. data-id; DEFAULT-DENY: only names on the STRUCTURAL_ATTRS allowlist keep values verbatim, every other valued attribute is placeholdered as untrusted text
protocolRules.§2.4 verification: findLeaks() returns per-violation findings; empty is the pass condition

cases-real.template.json.role: ten-key entry skeleton for a contributor

capture-helper.js.role: optional DevTools Console snippet that lists recognised post containers and saves one to ~/Downloads
capture-helper.js.note: Protocol section 1 (manual copy-paste) remains sufficient. This exists because the host has no xclip/xsel/wl-paste, so the clipboard route needs a workaround. It reads the already-rendered DOM, makes no network request, does not navigate or click, clones the node so the live page is not mutated, and is bounded to one post per invocation.
capture-helper.js.verificationDetail: Loaded into a real Chromium via the chrome-devtools MCP and executed against the synthetic fixture: 7 candidates found, index 3 correctly flagged suggested=true. Build output saved to disk and driven through sanitize.cjs to leak findings 0.

one-shot-capture.sh.role: One-command admission for the terminal half: discover capture -> sanitise -> verify zero leaks -> build the ten-key entry -> stage -> report protocol section 3 progress; --admit merges and runs the unmodified 071 gate
one-shot-capture.sh.safeByDefault: Entries go to plans/research/079/staged-entries.json (now gitignored). cases-real.json is never modified until --admit. --dry-run writes nothing.
doesNot: reach the browser or any LinkedIn session (no CDP endpoint exists, and section 1a permits only an owner-started session)
hand-patch markup: a leak finding aborts and tells the user to report the shape instead
one-shot-capture.sh.verifiedEndToEnd: Staged one positive and one body-mention negative built from a simulated capture, ran --admit, and the UNMODIFIED 071 gate passed 7/7 (2 per-entry detector outcomes + 5 gate tests: ten-key schema, scanRoot enum, provenance, id dedupe, sanitization). cases-real.json was then reverted to [] so no synthetic entry remains in the real corpus.
one-shot-capture.sh.guideMode: --guide prints the browser-side walkthrough; a missing capture file prints the same walkthrough instead of a bare pointer, because the terminal half cannot run before the browser half.
one-shot-capture.sh.gateFailureOutput: A failing --admit gate now prints the failing assertion names and the pass/fail counts, then interprets the failure: a 'scan matches expectedTarget' failure on a positive is mapped to the two known causes (label grammar, per F-01; container shape) so it is recorded as a finding rather than read as breakage.

capture-live.cjs.role: PRIMARY capture path. Connects over loopback CDP to a browser it launches (dedicated profile; the user's normal Chrome is never touched or closed), reads the posts already rendered, classifies them by Suggested label, extracts and sanitises in memory, and stages ten-key entries.
capture-live.cjs.protocolPosition: Single-shot, human-invoked, own-session, bounded to the section 3 minimum set - the form permitted by 071/protocol.md section 1a.
capture-live.cjs.autoDerivedLabel: The label phrase to preserve is derived from the captured header metadata (text up to a ' - ' separator), so the exact string the detector keys on survives without the user guessing it.
capture-live.cjs.verified: Exercised end to end against a synthetic fixture served on loopback with a throwaway Chrome on a debug port (never against LinkedIn): CDP connect, 7 candidates classified, the Suggested post correctly flagged, label auto-derived as 'Suggested for you', entries built, sanitised to 0 leaks, staged. Raw markup never written to disk. Not covered by the automated test suite because it requires a CDP browser; verified by that run.
capture-live.cjs.testHook: --url-match exists so the script can be pointed at a local fixture; it is the only reason that flag is a flag.

languageHandling.uiLocaleFromPage: document.documentElement.lang, normalised to a base subtag; becomes each entry's metadataLocale
languageHandling.labelSource: never guessed and never translated - either --suggested-label, or a value remembered per locale in ~/.cache/ss-capture-labels.json, or an interactive pick from the label strings actually found in post headers
languageHandling.degreeFilter: Connection degrees (bullet+ordinal) are excluded from the candidate list so the pick is short. Anchored on purpose: a trailing \b silently fails on Unicode ordinals such as 'º' because that character is not a word character to JavaScript's \b - a real bug found and fixed during testing.
languageHandling.expectationLogic: Whether an entry is a positive or a documented fail-open negative is derived from the project's DOCUMENTED intent (English-only labels; legacy-only enumeration), not from the detector's live behaviour - deriving it from live behaviour would make the gate a tautology and unable to catch a regression.
languageHandling.consequenceForNonEnglishUsers: A Spanish capture is recorded as a negative control asserting fail-open, and the gate passes. The non-English label is an explicitly required part of the 071 section 3 set, so the contribution is legitimate and necessary - it is the evidence needed before non-English labels could be added deliberately.

capture-live.cjs.reusesUserProfile: DEFAULT is the user's own Chrome user-data-dir and profile directory, so the existing LinkedIn session is reused and no login is needed. Chrome must be closed to attach to that profile; the script detects a running Chrome and offers to close+relaunch it (SIGTERM, 20s grace, aborts if it will not exit). --close-chrome/-y skip the question; --dedicated-profile keeps a throwaway profile; --attach uses an existing debug port.
capture-live.cjs.autoScroll: Scrolls the feed itself instead of asking the user to scroll and re-run. Dedupes candidates across rounds by HTML prefix because LinkedIn unmounts posts as they leave the viewport; stops when the feed stops growing, an accept predicate is met, or the scroll budget runs out (--max-scrolls, default 12). Progress is printed as 'N post(s) collected (scroll i/budget)'.
capture-live.cjs.diagnoseMode: --diagnose prints a selector census (per-family match counts, META_SELECTOR match count with an explicit 'matched NOTHING - that is the bug' callout, the distinct header strings, URL, UI locale) PLUS an element skeleton of the first posts: tag and class names only, never text. Class names are structural, not personal data, and they are exactly what is needed to fix a selector that no longer matches the live DOM.
capture-live.cjs.extensionsDisabledByDefault: Extensions are disabled during capture unless --with-extensions: a content script that rewrites the DOM (including this repo's own extension) makes the capture worse evidence about what LinkedIn rendered.
capture-live.cjs.scrollReporting: Honest stop reporting: gather() returns stepsRun and stoppedReason ('target-reached', 'feed-stopped-growing', or 'budget'), and the failure message distinguishes 'the feed stopped yielding new posts, so raising --max-scrolls will not help' from 'budget exhausted, try a larger one'. An earlier version hardcoded the budget into the message and claimed 'scrolled 12 times' after only four iterations -- a user reported the output as suspiciously fast, and the message was simply false.
capture-live.cjs.scrollMechanism: Growth is detected by the identity of the TAIL post changing, because LinkedIn unmounts posts as it mounts others so a raw count can stay flat while new content loads. Scrolling uses scrollIntoView on the last post rather than window.scrollBy, so it works whether LinkedIn scrolls the window or an inner container. An earlier version compared the deduped seen-count against the raw DOM count, which was incomparable and made the loop give up almost immediately.
capture-live.cjs.selectorOverride: --meta-selector SEL overrides the header-metadata selector. A selector validity pre-flight asks the browser's own parser, so an invalid selector names the CSS error; a valid-but-zero-match selector is reported explicitly rather than silently finding nothing.
capture-live.cjs.labelDetection: CLASS-INDEPENDENT. --diagnose on the reporting user's live feed showed LinkedIn now serves hashed atomic class names (gflljw, gflkzy, gflkxr, ...) that change every deploy, and that its two legacy post selectors match ZERO posts. Any class-based selector for the header slot is therefore worthless. The reader instead collects SHORT TEXT strings from every element in each post and matches the declared label by EXACT equality, which is deploy-proof and language-proof. --meta-selector remains available as an additive source.

capture-live.test.cjs.role: Offline tests for the language handling (no browser needed): degree detection across locales, label clustering, and the positive/fail-open-negative decision.

coreInvariant: Vocabulary check, not a name denylist: every alphanumeric run in every text node and every text-bearing attribute must be either the placeholder token or a declared label.

protocolDeviation.clause: 071/protocol.md §2.3 words the urn sentinel as shape urn:li:activity:71XX
protocolDeviation.deviation: This implementation preserves the urn entity kind (urn:li:company:71XX stays a company urn) instead of collapsing every kind to 'activity'.
protocolDeviation.reason: POST_SELECTORS matches the literal substring 'urn:li:activity:'. Collapsing a company payload to an activity payload would make a capture match a selector it never matched, i.e. fabricate a positive — the exact failure 071/protocol.md forbids ('fabricated provenance poisons the very gate this plan serves'). Sentinel shape is preserved; only the kind is retained.
protocolDeviation.enforcement: findLeaks enforces the 71 sentinel prefix on any urn:li value regardless of kind.

endToEndProof.result: 071 gate exit 0, 5/5 tests pass: ten-key schema, scanRoot enum, provenance user-contributed, validationStatus real-donated, id dedupe against 068's ten, sanitization check, and per-entry detector outcomes (positive targeted, negative fails open).
endToEndProof.also: 068's unmodified detector still returns exactly the post for the sanitised positive and zero targets for the sanitised body-mention negative.
endToEndProof.reproduce: node --test plans/research/079/sanitize.test.cjs (test 'end-to-end: a sanitised capture satisfies the existing plan-071 gate')

selfExposedGap.what: The first test pass exposed a hole in this module's own design: attributes outside a known-text list kept their values verbatim, so PII could hide in an unrecognised attribute and pass both sanitise AND verify — the same class of gap as Step 0.
selfExposedGap.fix: Default-deny STRUCTURAL_ATTRS allowlist; every non-allowlisted valued attribute is placeholdered as untrusted text, and findLeaks checks it.
selfExposedGap.rationale: Recorded rather than hidden because it is the same failure mode this plan criticises in the 071 gate, and the fix is the reason the verifier can be trusted.

documentedLimitations: URL paths are preserved: query and fragment are stripped and known identity slugs are rewritten, but the rest of a path survives. Host and route are structural evidence and LinkedIn media paths are opaque CDN hashes. A URL whose path spelled out a human name would not be caught. No heuristic was added because a name-shaped-slug guess would false-positive on ordinary paths and block legitimate donations.
The STRUCTURAL_ATTRS allowlist is not exhaustive; an attribute whose value must survive but is not listed will be placeholdered. This fails visibly in the detector outcome, never silently.

Sanitisation is a text-and-identity transformation, not a proof of non-identification. A capture still reveals that some post existed with some structure at some time; contributors are told to capture only the post container, never anything above it.

governanceAmendment.what: 071/protocol.md section 1.3 was re-specified (not deleted) into a narrowly bounded authorized-collector class (section 1a). Forward-only; 071/verdict.json is NOT edited.
governanceAmendment.effectOnThisPlan: None mechanically. The contributor path, the sanitiser, the leak verifier, the ten-key entry schema and 071 section 3 minimums are all unchanged. The exception is owner-only and does not alter the provenance class.

protocolRulesUpdated.labelMatching: Phrase-level, not token-level. Declared label phrases are preserved verbatim wherever they appear; only the remainder is placeholdered. Fixes a defect where realistic metadata such as 'Suggested for you - Acme' reduced to 'Placeholder - Placeholder' and destroyed the exact string the detector keys on.
protocolRulesUpdated.footgun: --label is a declaration of trust: a declared phrase is preserved AND accepted by the verifier, because the verifier checks against the declared set. Declaring a person's name would leak it and pass the leak check. The CLI now echoes declared phrases with an explicit warning, the behaviour is pinned by a test, and the guide states the rule. No heuristic name-detector is used by design: a guess would false-positive on ordinary metadata and block legitimate donations.
protocolRulesUpdated.caseMarker: A missing data-case marker is now injected at admission time via --case-marker, so a Route A manual copy does not need a hand edit for expectedTarget to resolve. Injected AFTER the section 2.2 fingerprint check, so it is deliberately outside the sanitisation guarantee; idempotent when the marker is already present (Route B). Marker ids are restricted to [A-Za-z0-9._-]+ so no escaping is needed.

findings.claim: The 068 prototype detector and the shared matchesLabel grammar accept ONLY 'Suggested' or 'Suggested <middot> <sponsor>'. A header rendering as 'Suggested for you' (or 'Suggested for you <middot> <sponsor>') yields ZERO targets: a silent false negative, not an error.
findings.classification: SOURCE-VERIFIED (grammar behaviour), UNKNOWN (whether LinkedIn renders a fuller label)
findings.reproduce: node -e with jsdom + plans/research/068/detector.cjs; matchesLabel('Suggested for you', ['Suggested']) === false; scanSuggested over a legacy-shaped container with that label text returns 0 targets
findings.disposition: DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED. 071/protocol.md section 4 requires labels to be established by capture and forbids guessing them; 068/detector.cjs:29-31 states the English-only no-guess policy. The first real capture adjudicates: a failing expectedTarget on a genuine entry IS the finding (protocol section 5).
findings.actionability: high - the first donated capture will immediately confirm or clear this, because the gate asserts expectedTarget.

findings.claim: Label matching was token-wise, so a combined label such as 'Suggested for you <middot> Acme' was reduced to 'Placeholder <middot> Placeholder', destroying the signal.
findings.disposition: FIXED - phrase-level matching; verified 'Suggested for you <middot> Acme' -> 'Suggested for you <middot> Placeholder'.

findings.claim: A JSON-quoted capture file failed with a bare 'unparsable tag' message, and non-markup input was equally opaque.
findings.disposition: FIXED - the CLI auto-unwraps a JSON-quoted string and non-markup input returns an explicit, actionable error.

findings.claim: sanitizeText reported changed:true when the replacement was byte-identical, which would have made the idempotence property report phantom changes.

On the reporting user's live LinkedIn feed, both legacy post selectors match ZERO posts: '[data-id*="urn:li:activity:"]' = 0 and '.feed-shared-update-v2' = 0 out of 16 detected posts. The third POST_SELECTORS entry, 'article', also matched 0. Only the modern '[data-testid="mainFeed"] [role="listitem"]' shape matched (16).
findings.classification: OBSERVED (selector counts, via --diagnose against the user's own feed) + SOURCE-VERIFIED (the selector values at content.js:34-48)
findings.evidence: post candidates per selector family: 0 [data-id*=urn:li:activity:], 0 .feed-shared-update-v2, 16 [data-testid=mainFeed] [role=listitem], 0 article; header-meta elements matched by META_SELECTOR: 0
findings.implication: scanForBlockedAuthors and scanForLabeledPosts enumerate ONLY via AUTHOR_BLOCK_SELECTORS (content.js:45-48), so on this feed shape the author blocklist and the opt-in Promoted filter have nothing to enumerate. The 068 detector's POST_SELECTOR is the same pair, so it cannot target anything either.
findings.uncertainty: LinkedIn A/B-tests layouts, so this is a property of one account at one time and must not be generalised to all users. Text-based bait blocking uses a selector-free sibling heuristic FIRST (shared/post-container.js:44-99), which may still resolve containers, so bait blocking is not necessarily broken - only the selector-based passes are demonstrably empty. Whether the manual-control gate still passes depends on '[data-testid="expandable-text-box"]', which could NOT be measured on the synthetic fixture because it does not model that element.
findings.consistency: This is consistent with AGENTS.md:146: the modern React shape was known only from competitor source because there were 'no first-hand authenticated LinkedIn samples'. It is now measured on a real feed.
findings.disposition: REPORTED, deliberately not fixed. Changing production selectors is out of scope for this research plan and must be gated on a real capture - which is exactly what this pipeline now produces. A production plan should follow.
